_comment: Documented, publicly reported cyber incidents. Factual summaries only; each carries a source URL and a confidence level. 'signals' are the externally-observable entry conditions Aegis can compare against (empty = library-only, e.g. supply-chain or phishing we cannot see from an external scan). Techniques are MITRE ATT&CK ids.

incidents.name: WannaCry
incidents.initial_access: Spread automatically by exploiting the SMBv1 'EternalBlue' flaw (MS17-010) on unpatched Windows systems reachable over the network.
incidents.impact: Over 200,000 computers across 150 countries; the NHS cancelled around 19,000 appointments.
controls: Apply MS17-010 and keep Windows patched
Never expose TCP 445 to the internet

incidents.name: NotPetya
incidents.initial_access: A trojanised update of Ukrainian accounting software (M.E.Doc) planted the malware, which then spread using EternalBlue (SMBv1) and stolen credentials.
incidents.impact: Estimated 10+ billion USD in global damage; Maersk rebuilt ~4,000 servers and 45,000 PCs.
controls: Segment networks to limit lateral movement

incidents.name: Equifax breach
incidents.initial_access: Exploited an unpatched Apache Struts flaw (CVE-2017-5638) on a public-facing web application; a patch had been available for two months.
incidents.impact: Personal data of ~147 million people exposed; ~700 million USD settlement.
controls: Inventory public apps and their components

incidents.name: Microsoft Exchange (ProxyLogon)
incidents.initial_access: A chain starting with CVE-2021-26855 (SSRF) let attackers authenticate to internet-facing on-premises Exchange servers and run code.
incidents.impact: At least 30,000 US organisations and many more worldwide compromised before patching.
controls: Avoid exposing Exchange directly; front with a gateway/VPN
Hunt for web shells after exposure

incidents.name: Log4Shell exploitation
incidents.initial_access: CVE-2021-44228 in the Log4j logging library allowed remote code execution by sending a crafted string to any public-facing app that logged it.
incidents.impact: One of the most widespread vulnerabilities ever; exploited within days across the internet.
controls: Keep a software bill of materials to find affected apps fast

incidents.name: MOVEit Transfer mass hack
incidents.initial_access: A SQL-injection zero-day (CVE-2023-34362) in the internet-facing MOVEit Transfer file-transfer app allowed data theft.
incidents.impact: Data from 2,000+ organisations and 60+ million individuals stolen.
controls: Limit who can reach such apps from the internet
Have an incident plan for third-party-software zero-days

incidents.name: Colonial Pipeline
incidents.initial_access: Attackers logged into a legacy VPN account using a leaked password; the account had no multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Largest US fuel pipeline shut down for days; ~4.4 million USD ransom paid (partly recovered).
controls: Require MFA on every remote-access/VPN account
Monitor remote logins for unusual locations

incidents.name: Change Healthcare
incidents.initial_access: Attackers used stolen credentials on a Citrix remote-access portal that was not protected by multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Massive disruption to US healthcare claims and pharmacy processing; data on an estimated 100 million people affected.
controls: Enforce MFA on every remote-access gateway

incidents.name: Hof van Twente municipality
incidents.initial_access: Attackers reached an exposed remote-desktop (RDP) server and guessed a weak admin password ('Welkom2020'); there was no multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Systems and backups wiped; recovery cost estimated around 4.2 million EUR. A well-documented Dutch case.
controls: Never expose RDP to the internet; put it behind a VPN
Require MFA and strong passwords for remote access

incidents.name: Maastricht University
incidents.initial_access: A phishing email gave the attackers a foothold; they moved laterally over weeks and deployed Clop ransomware, partly via an unpatched server.
incidents.impact: Most systems encrypted just before the holidays; the university paid ~197,000 EUR ransom.
controls: Patch internal servers, not just internet-facing ones

incidents.name: SolarWinds (SUNBURST)
incidents.initial_access: Attackers inserted a backdoor into SolarWinds Orion software updates, which thousands of customers then installed themselves.
incidents.impact: ~18,000 organisations received the trojanised update; a smaller number were further targeted.
controls: Vet software suppliers and update integrity
Monitor outbound traffic from management tools

incidents.name: MGM Resorts
incidents.initial_access: Attackers (Scattered Spider) phoned the IT help desk, impersonated an employee and got identity/MFA reset, then accessed Okta and Azure.
incidents.impact: Days of disruption to hotels and casinos; estimated ~100 million USD impact.
controls: Strong help-desk identity verification before resets
Limit what a single identity can reach

incidents.name: Snowflake customer account compromises
incidents.initial_access: Attackers logged into customer cloud-data accounts using credentials stolen earlier by infostealer malware; the accounts lacked multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Data stolen from around 165 customer environments and used for extortion.
controls: Enforce MFA on all cloud/SaaS accounts

incidents.name: Marriott / Starwood
incidents.initial_access: Attackers had long-term, undetected access to the Starwood guest-reservation database (since around 2014, before Marriott's acquisition).
incidents.impact: Data of up to ~339 million guest records exposed; large GDPR fine by the UK ICO.
controls: Protect and monitor databases holding personal data

incidents.name: Capital One
incidents.initial_access: A server-side request forgery against a misconfigured web application firewall let the attacker reach cloud metadata and then read S3 storage.
incidents.impact: Data of ~100 million US and ~6 million Canadian customers exposed; ~80 million USD regulatory penalty.
controls: Fix WAF/app misconfigurations and test for SSRF

incidents.name: Kaseya VSA
incidents.initial_access: REvil exploited a zero-day in the internet-facing Kaseya VSA remote-management server to push ransomware to downstream customers.
incidents.impact: Up to ~1,500 downstream businesses hit through managed service providers.
controls: Don't expose RMM consoles to the internet
